title: Normal-kernel invariants as rational modules for an affine fppf quotient
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Let $K,H,Q$ be flat affine finitely presented group schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-flat-morphism], with homomorphisms $K\to H\xrightarrow{\pi}Q$. Assume that $K=H\times_{Q,e_Q}\operatorname{Spec}A$, that $\pi$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation, and that $Q$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf $H/K$; fppf covers are jointly surjective families of flat locally finitely presented morphisms. For any of these groups $J$, put $C_J=\Gamma(J,\mathcal O_J)$ with the coordinate Hopf algebra maps induced by multiplication, identity and inverse, as in [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra]. A rational $J$-module is an arbitrary $A$-module $V$ with an $A$-linear coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_A C_J$ satisfying counit and coassociativity; tensor products are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Write $V^J=\{v:\rho_V(v)=v\otimes1\}$. An equivariant linear map commutes with coactions. Inflation of a rational $Q$-module means composing its coaction with $1\otimes\pi^*:V\otimes_A C_Q\to V\otimes_A C_H$.
For every rational $H$-module $V$, the submodule $N=V^K=\ker(\rho_{V|K}-(v\mapsto v\otimes1))$ has a unique rational $Q$-module structure whose inflation makes $N\hookrightarrow V$ equivariant. Every $H$-equivariant map $V\to V'$ restricts to a $Q$-equivariant map $V^K\to(V')^K$. For any rational $Q$-module $W$, inflation satisfies $(\operatorname{Inf}_\pi W)^H=W^Q$ as submodules of $W$; for any two rational $Q$-modules, an $A$-linear map is $Q$-equivariant if and only if it is $H$-equivariant after inflation. No finiteness or flatness is required of $V,V',W$ or $N$, and $K$ need not be smooth or reduced.

source.place: Proposition 9.5.1 proof, printed p.525: the fully faithful pullback j^* along BH to BQ and kernel-invariant direct image j_*; the rational-module form of that descent input. Local PDF WANTED; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf

proof.text: Put $B=C_H$, $D=C_K$, $C=C_Q$ and $u=\pi^*:C\to B$. Apply the affine flatness criterion to the whole affine schemes: $B,D,C$ are flat $A$-modules and $u$ is flat. Since $\pi$ is surjective, the flat-surjective-spectrum criterion makes $u$ faithfully flat. These applications use flatness of the three structural morphisms and faithful flatness of $\pi$, not flatness of a representation module.

Use the coordinate Hopf description to evaluate a coaction at points: for an $A$-algebra $S$ and $h:B\to S$, set $h\cdot(v\otimes s)=\sum v_i\otimes h(b_i)s$ when $\rho_V(v)=\sum v_i\otimes b_i$. The counit and coassociativity identities give $e\cdot x=x$ and $h\cdot(h'\cdot x)=(hh')\cdot x$; the inverse gives the inverse operator. Equality at the universal point $B\to B$ is precisely equality of coaction maps. The scheme-theoretic kernel hypothesis gives $\pi(h^{-1}kh)=e$, so $h^{-1}kh\in K(S)$. It also gives mutually inverse morphisms
$$H\times_AK\longrightarrow H\times_QH,\quad(h,k)\longmapsto(h,hk),\qquad(h_1,h_2)\longmapsto(h_1,h_1^{-1}h_2).$$
They are morphisms because multiplication and inversion are, and the second component of the inverse factors through the defining kernel fibre product. The two composites are identities by cancellation. Thus $B\otimes_CB$ identifies with $B\otimes_AD$, with the two projections corresponding to $h$ and $hk$.

source.place: Tag 022S, group-scheme laws; direct evaluation and kernel fibre-product calculation

proof.text: Write $d=\rho_{V|K}-(v\mapsto v\otimes1)$ and $i:N=\ker d\hookrightarrow V$. Tensor the exact sequence $0\to N\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{d}V\otimes_AD$ with any flat $A$-algebra $S$. Exactness gives an injection $i_S:N\otimes_AS\hookrightarrow V\otimes_AS$ with image exactly $\ker(d\otimes1_S)=(V\otimes_AS)^{K_S}$. Here the latter invariants mean the kernel of the base-changed coaction minus the trivial coaction, under the tensor associativity and symmetry identifications. This is only a flat-base-change assertion. In particular it applies to $S=B$ and $S=D$. Also every image of $n\in N$ is fixed by every $k\in K(T)$ for every $A$-algebra $T$: evaluate the original equality $\rho_{V|K}(n)=n\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), applied to the defining kernel sequence

proof.text:
For $n\in N$ take $h\in H(B)$ to be the universal point. Over $T=B\otimes_AD$ let $k\in K(T)$ be universal and extend $h$ to $T$. Normality from step 2 and the last equality of step 3 give
$$k\cdot(h\cdot n)=h\cdot((h^{-1}kh)\cdot n)=h\cdot n.$$
This is exactly $(d\otimes1_B)(\rho_V(n))=0$, with the tensor factors reordered. Step 3 therefore factors $\rho_V i$ uniquely as $(i\otimes1_B)\alpha$ for an $A$-linear map $\alpha:N\to N\otimes_AB$. The counit identity for $\alpha$ follows after $i$; its coassociativity follows after $i\otimes1_B\otimes1_B$, injective by applying flat tensor exactness twice. Both then reduce to the corresponding identities of $\rho_V$. Likewise, after the injection $i\otimes1_D$, its restriction to $K$ is $n\mapsto n\otimes1$; hence $K$ acts trivially on this rational $H$-module $N$.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat); Tag 022S, conjugation identity at universal points

proof.text:
Under the isomorphism $H\times_AK\simeq H\times_QH$ of step 2, the two pullbacks of $\alpha(n)$ are equal: they are $h\cdot n$ and $(hk)\cdot n=h\cdot(k\cdot n)=h\cdot n$, since the restriction of $\alpha$ to $K$ is trivial. This equality is in $N\otimes_AB\otimes_AD$, using the coaction laws for $\alpha$ itself. Apply Amitsur exactness to the faithfully flat ring map $C\to B$ and the $C$-module $M=N\otimes_AC$. It identifies $M$ with the equalizer of
$$N\otimes_AB\rightrightarrows N\otimes_A(B\otimes_CB).$$
Consequently there is a unique element $\beta(n)\in N\otimes_AC$ mapping to $\alpha(n)$. Injectivity of the augmentation shows that these elements depend $A$-linearly on $n$, defining $\beta:N\to N\otimes_AC$ with $(1\otimes u)\beta=\alpha$. No flatness of $M$ is needed in the cited theorem.

source.place: Tag 023M (lemma-ff-exact), exactness at the augmentation and first differential

proof.text: For every $A$-module $X$, the same Amitsur theorem with $M=X\otimes_AC$ makes $j_X=1_X\otimes u:X\otimes_AC\to X\otimes_AB$ injective. Applying this twice, first to $X=N\otimes_AC$ and then to $X=N\otimes_AB$, and reordering factors, makes $1_N\otimes u\otimes u$ injective. Since $\pi$ is a group homomorphism, $u$ respects comultiplication and counit. Thus the two sides of the coassociativity equation for $\beta$ become those of $\alpha$ after this injection, and its counit equation is the counit equation for $\alpha$. So $\beta$ is a rational $Q$-coaction. Its inflation is $\alpha$, making $i$ equivariant. Any other coaction with this property agrees after $N\otimes_AC\xrightarrow{j_N}N\otimes_AB\xrightarrow{i\otimes1_B}V\otimes_AB$; both arrows are injective, the second by flat tensor exactness. Hence the coaction is unique.

source.place: Tags 023M (lemma-ff-exact), 00HD (lemma-flat), 022S; descent of the coaction equations

proof.text: If $f:V\to V'$ is $H$-equivariant, restriction of its coaction equation to $K$ gives $d'f(n)=(f\otimes1_D)d(n)=0$ for $n\in N$. Hence it restricts to an $A$-linear map $f_N:N\to N'=(V')^K$. The two sides of its $Q$-equivariance equation agree after $N'\otimes_AC\to N'\otimes_AB\to V'\otimes_AB$, by the original $H$-equivariance equation and the construction of $\beta,\beta'$. These arrows are injective by Amitsur exactness and flat tensor exactness, respectively. Thus $f_N$ is $Q$-equivariant. Restrictions preserve identities and composition because their underlying maps are the original restrictions.

source.place: Tags 023M (lemma-ff-exact) and 00HD (lemma-flat), applied to the equivariance equation

proof.text:
For a rational $Q$-module $W$, its inflated coaction is $(1\otimes u)\rho_W$. The equation for an $H$-fixed element is therefore
$$j_W(\rho_W(w)-w\otimes1)=0.$$
Injectivity of $j_W$ from Amitsur exactness makes this equivalent to $\rho_W(w)=w\otimes1$, proving equality of the two invariant submodules of $W$. For an $A$-linear map $a:W\to W'$ between rational $Q$-modules, the difference of the two sides of its coaction equation lies in $W'\otimes_AC$; after $j_{W'}$ it is exactly the difference of the two inflated equations. The same injection proves that $a$ is $Q$-equivariant if and only if its inflation is $H$-equivariant. All tensor injections used were supplied by flat coordinate algebras or Amitsur exactness for arbitrary modules. There was no finite-generation, smoothness or reducedness argument.

source.place: Tag 023M (lemma-ff-exact), injectivity of the augmentation for arbitrary modules
